ideas.title: Batch Book for Small Cosmetics and Soap Makers

notes.stateful: The maker keeps materials, recipes, supplier lots, batches and cost history and returns to them every production day.
notes.connected: Imports supplier lots and Etsy or Shopify order exports by CSV so orders link to batches, and exports everything as CSV and printable batch records.
notes.unattended: A daily email lists materials below their reorder point and lots that expire within 30 days.
notes.engine: Consumes lots oldest-first or earliest-expiry across several lots with unit conversion, prices each batch from the lots actually used, and traces a supplier lot to every batch and order made from it.

buildPlan.title: Recipe to batch
buildPlan.delivers: Sign in, add materials and a recipe, record a batch that deducts stock and shows a batch code in the maker's format.
buildPlan.acceptance: A 10-bar batch deducts the exact grams from stock and shows a code in the chosen format; deployed.

buildPlan.title: Lots, oldest first
buildPlan.delivers: Receive lots with supplier batch number, cost and expiry; a batch draws from the oldest or earliest-expiring lot first.
buildPlan.acceptance: A batch larger than the first lot splits across two lots, checked by a unit test.

buildPlan.title: Actual cost
buildPlan.delivers: Cost per batch and per unit from the lots used, including packaging and unit conversion between grams, ounces and millilitres.
buildPlan.acceptance: Matches a hand-worked fixture to the cent.

buildPlan.title: Recall view and batch record
buildPlan.delivers: Pick a supplier lot and see every batch made from it; print a batch record page for the product information file.
buildPlan.acceptance: A fixture with three batches over two lots returns exactly the right batches, and the printed record lists every lot used.

buildPlan.title: Reorder and expiry digest
buildPlan.delivers: A reorder point per material and a scheduled daily email of materials to reorder and lots near expiry.
buildPlan.acceptance: An email is sent only when a threshold is crossed, and lists the right materials.

buildPlan.title: Order import and full export
buildPlan.delivers: Import an Etsy or Shopify order CSV to link orders to batches; export every record as CSV for safekeeping.
buildPlan.acceptance: A sample Etsy CSV links its orders without duplicates on re-import, and the export imports again cleanly.

buildPlan.title: Polish
buildPlan.delivers: Business-owner README, phone layout for the workshop, keyboard and screen-reader pass, walkthrough test.
buildPlan.acceptance: A walkthrough test runs sign-in to recall view; axe reports no serious issues.

ideas.summary: A batch book for solo cosmetics and soap makers who sell on Etsy and at markets: ingredient lots used oldest-first, a batch code for each label, the true cost of every batch and a recall view, for far less than the incumbent's lot-tracking plan.

public.summary: Keep a proper batch record for every batch you make, with the real cost of each one, without a spreadsheet.
public.problem: You make soap, balms or creams in small batches, and every label needs a batch number you can trace back. You want to know which jar of oil or bag of butter went into which batch, and what that batch really cost you. The tools that do this either cost a lot each month or only work if you sell on one platform, so you end up with a spreadsheet you don't trust.
public.forWhom: Solo and small cosmetics and soap makers who sell on Etsy, at markets and on their own website.
benefits: A batch code for every label, ready to print
Know exactly what each batch cost you
Find every batch made from a faulty ingredient in seconds
A reminder before you run out or an ingredient expires
Records you can export and keep for years

ideas.problemStatement: Cosmetics makers in Great Britain and the EU must put a batch number on every label and keep a product information file for ten years after the last batch, and every maker wants to know what each batch really cost and which supplier lot went into it; the tool many of them used raised its price and puts lot tracking on a $99-a-month plan, so they fall back to spreadsheets.
ideas.description: The maker enters materials and recipes once, then receives each purchase as a lot with the supplier's batch number, cost and expiry date. Recording a production run consumes lots oldest-first, gives the batch a code for the label and prices the batch from the lots actually used. A recall view lists every batch, and every Etsy or market order linked by CSV import, made from a given supplier lot, and each batch prints as a record for the product information file. A daily email warns of materials to reorder and lots about to expire, and everything exports as CSV.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo and micro cosmetics and soap makers (1 to 5 people) in Great Britain and the EU who sell on Etsy, at markets and on their own non-Shopify websites.
ideas.buyer: The maker, from the business's own card; a small monthly subscription.
ideas.whyNow: Stocksmith (Craftybase under a new name since July 2026) keeps batch and lot tracking on its Indie plan at $99 a month; four Shopify-only batch and lot apps launched between July and October 2026 show the demand but leave Etsy and market sellers out; and Great Britain's cosmetics rules require a batch identification number on the label and a product information file kept 10 years after the last batch.

problemEvidence.author: poster A (US soap and cosmetics maker following GMP, about 3 years on the app)
problemEvidence.summary: Needed stock tracked per lot and used first-in first-out for GMP; even the top tier did not do it, and the price was rising from $34.99 to $79 a month, so they were looking for another system.

problemEvidence.author: Stocksmith (vendor)
problemEvidence.summary: Batch and lot tracking and traceability reports appear only from the Indie plan at $99 a month ($83 billed yearly); Pro from $20 and Studio $49 do not include lots (read 2026-11-22).

problemEvidence.author: BatchMakes (vendor)
problemEvidence.summary: A web app for makers sells its lot register, lot traceability and recall reports only on Business at 59 EUR a month plus VAT; the free plan has recipes, batches and costs but no lots (read 2026-11-22).

problemEvidence.author: UK government (regulator)
problemEvidence.summary: A cosmetic label must carry an identification number such as a batch number, the product information file must be kept 10 years after the last batch, and a sole trader can be the Responsible Person; no small-business exemption.

problemEvidence.author: US FDA (regulator)
problemEvidence.summary: Small businesses are exempt from GMP, registration and listing under MoCRA, while adverse-event reports and safety records still apply; for US makers a batch record is good practice, not a duty, which narrows the buyer to Great Britain and the EU.

competitors.name: Stocksmith (formerly Craftybase)
competitors.price: Pro from $20 a month; Studio $49; Indie $99 ($83 billed yearly); Business $199; Growth $349
competitors.gap: Has batch and lot tracking, first-in first-out and recall lookup, but only from the $99 Indie plan.

competitors.name: BatchMakes
competitors.price: Free for one user; Business 59 EUR a month plus VAT
competitors.gap: Lot register and recall reports only on the 59-euro plan; first-in first-out lot use not mentioned; no Etsy integration.

competitors.name: Inventora
competitors.price: Starter $23 a month (500 materials)
competitors.gap: Lists 'Full Batch Traceability' and syncs with Etsy, but its help pages do not describe supplier lots, first-in first-out use or expiry.

competitors.name: MakerPantry
competitors.price: Free, $19, $39, $69 a month; 0 reviews
competitors.gap: Tracks ingredient lots first-in first-out, but keeps no batch records or codes and works only on Shopify.

competitors.name: Batchready
competitors.price: Free; 0 reviews
competitors.gap: Batch numbers, best-before dates and a recall record, but no ingredient lots or costing, and Shopify only.

competitors.name: Soap batch tracker spreadsheet
competitors.gap: A batch log and cost per bar with no lot tracking or recall view.

keyFeatures: Ingredient lots with supplier batch number, cost and expiry
Batches that use lots oldest-first and get a label code
Actual cost per batch and per unit
Recall view from a supplier lot to every batch and order
Daily reorder and expiry email
Printable batch record and full CSV export

features: Batch recording with oldest-first lot use and a batch code
Batch record print and CSV export
outOfScope: Live Etsy or Shopify sync (CSV import first)

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind front end; Supabase sign-in and a per-app schema for materials, lots, batches and orders; a scheduled job and transactional email for the daily digest; CSV parsing and PDF batch records in the browser.

pricing.model: Monthly or yearly subscription per maker
pricing.rationale: Well under Inventora's $23, BatchMakes' 59 euros and Stocksmith's $99 lot plan, and above the cheap Shopify-only tools that have no lots, because it adds costing and the lot-to-batch trace off Shopify.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 120 makers x $12 a month = $1,440 a month. Assumes makers in Great Britain and the EU find it by search for batch codes and batch records; search volume and conversion are unknown.
ideas.distribution: First 10: a free 'cosmetic batch code generator' and 'soap batch record template' page found by search, leading to the paid app; Etsy has no app store, so search is the channel. soapmakingforum.com returned 403 to this run and its promotion rule was not found: rule unknown, check before posting. Never post in the evidence thread.

validationTest.method: A landing page offering 'Batch Book: lot-tracked batch records and the true cost of every batch' with a '$12 a month, start' button and the free batch-code tool, promoted for 14 days by search ads on 'soap batch record template', 'cosmetic batch code' and 'lot tracking soap software' in Great Britain and the EU; no outreach to anyone.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 300 visitors, at least 4% price-button clicks and at least 10 email sign-ups in 14 days.
validationTest.cost: About $100 in ads plus a domain and one day of work.

ideas.moat: A maker's lots, recipes and years of batch records live in the app, and a 10-year record duty makes switching costly; the oldest-first lot engine with costing is more than a spreadsheet template.
compliance: Cosmetics law (GB and EU): the duties fall on the maker; the app supports batch codes and the product information file but must never claim to make anyone compliant.
Records retention: promise and deliver full export, because the product information file must be kept 10 years after the last batch.
UK GDPR and GDPR if customer names arrive with order imports: minimise and allow deletion.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the app.

risks.risk: BatchMakes or Inventora moves lots to a cheaper plan.
risks.mitigation: Compete on oldest-first costing and the batch record for Etsy and market sellers, at a lower price.

risks.risk: Makers fear losing years of records if the service closes.
risks.mitigation: One-click full export from day one and a stated retention policy.

risks.risk: Demand is thin: the only complaint found is from 2023.
risks.mitigation: Run the ad and landing-page test before building beyond milestone 1.

scoreRationale.pain: One dated complaint about missing lot and first-in first-out tracking, from 2023-09-05, by a US maker with no federal batch duty (https://apps.shopify.com/stocksmith-inventory-manufacturing/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest; https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/cosmetics-laws-regulations/modernization-cosmetics-regulation-act-2022-mocra); none found within 90 days.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Vendors charge for exactly this: Stocksmith's lot plan at $99 a month (https://stocksmith.io/pricing/), BatchMakes at 59 euros (https://batchmakes.com/pricing), and the complainant paid $34.99 for about three years.
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve search for batch-code and batch-record tools is the channel, and the incumbent already competes on that content (https://stocksmith.io/blog/batch-tracking).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: BatchMakes (https://batchmakes.com/pricing) and Inventora with Etsy sync from $23 (https://www.inventora.com/pricing-plans/) already sell traceability off Shopify; only a cheaper, oldest-first, cosmetics-focused tool is left.
scoreRationale.feasibility: A standalone web app with CSV import, a lot-consumption engine and a daily email; small vendors ship parts of it (https://apps.shopify.com/makerpantry).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: The legal duties fall on the maker, not the tool, but it must keep and export records for years (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/making-cosmetic-products-available-to-consumers-in-great-britain).

review.findings: Researched as a materials-cost and lot book after the spend pass found Stocksmith's paid plans and its 2023 low reviews. The adversarial reviewer cut the total from 18 to 16: pain 3 to 2 (one complaint, from 2023, by a US maker with no legal batch duty, and Stocksmith has since added first-in first-out and expiry on its $99 plan) and competitiveGap 2 to 1 (BatchMakes sells a lot register and recall reports off Shopify for 59 euros, and Inventora lists full batch traceability with Etsy sync from $23). It confirmed that BatchMakes' free plan has no lots, that four Shopify-only batch or lot apps exist, and that the legal driver applies to cosmetics makers in Great Britain and the EU, not to US soap and candle makers. Re-scoped to those makers, with oldest-first lots, label codes, actual cost per batch, a recall view from Etsy order imports and a batch-record export.

missing: pain 2 is below 4: the only complaint is from 2023-09-05, by a maker with no legal batch duty, and none was found within 90 days
gateGap.closedBy: The 14-day ad test with the free batch-code tool: 10 or more sign-ups and 4% price-button clicks from Great Britain and EU makers would show the pain the evidence lacks (pain 3); reaching 22 would also need a dated maker complaint within 90 days and a clearer gap below BatchMakes and Inventora, so validated is out of reach without new evidence.

ideas.title: Pickup Choice Keeper for One-Location Shopify Shops

notes.stateful: Each shop's rules are saved and revisited: which products are pickup-only, the pickup location and the message shoppers see.
notes.connected: A public Shopify app: Admin API for products and tags, a checkout validation function, and the Storefront API pickup preference set from the theme.
notes.engine: Cart rules for pickup-only, mixed and ship-only carts, the location-stock rule that decides whether pickup is offered at all, and express-checkout paths that skip the cart.
notes.shared: The merchant sets the rules and the message; the shopper receives checkout opened on pickup and a clear message when Ship cannot apply.

buildPlan.title: Block Ship with a message
buildPlan.delivers: Install on a dev store, tag pickup-only products, and a validation function blocks the Ship path with the merchant's own message.
buildPlan.acceptance: A cart with a tagged item and Ship selected cannot complete checkout and shows the message; an untagged cart checks out; deployed.

buildPlan.title: Carry the cart choice into checkout
buildPlan.delivers: Read the pickup choice the theme or a calendar app already writes as a cart attribute, and set the Storefront API pickup preference when the shopper clicks Checkout.
buildPlan.acceptance: Checkout opens on Pick up at the shop's location in at least 9 of 10 runs on desktop and phone; on failure it falls back to Ship with the validation message.

buildPlan.title: Live cart notice
buildPlan.delivers: A theme block for the cart page and drawer that explains pickup-only items and updates without a page reload.
buildPlan.acceptance: The notice appears and disappears without a refresh in Dawn and one other free theme.

buildPlan.title: Mixed carts, stock and express checkout
buildPlan.delivers: Rules for mixed carts and the location-stock condition, with express-checkout paths covered by validation.
buildPlan.acceptance: A test matrix passes: pickup-only, ship-only, mixed, out of stock at the location, and Shop Pay and Apple Pay buttons.

buildPlan.title: Billing and App Store readiness
buildPlan.delivers: A billing plan with trial, mandatory privacy webhooks, uninstall cleanup and the listing.
buildPlan.acceptance: A test charge is approved on a dev store and the privacy webhooks return 200.

buildPlan.title: Polish
buildPlan.delivers: Business-owner README, phone layout for settings, accessible notice (announced to screen readers, contrast passes), walkthrough test.
buildPlan.acceptance: A walkthrough test runs install to a pickup order; axe reports no serious issues.

ideas.summary: For one-location Shopify bakeries, butchers and food shops on Basic or Grow: keep the pickup choice a shopper made in the cart when they reach checkout, and stop pickup-only items being ordered for shipping, with a clear message.

public.summary: When a customer chooses pickup in your cart, checkout stays on pickup, and items you can't ship can't be ordered for delivery by mistake.
public.problem: You sell cakes, fresh meat or other items customers must collect, next to things you post. A customer picks collection in the cart, then checkout switches them back to delivery or shows a confusing error. Some give up, and some place an order you can't fulfil.
public.forWhom: Small shops on Shopify with one shop or kitchen where customers collect some items and others are posted.
benefits: Customers who choose pickup stay on pickup
No more orders for items you can't post
A clear message in your own words when delivery isn't possible
Fewer abandoned checkouts and refund emails

ideas.problemStatement: Shoppers choose collection in the cart, but checkout starts on Ship; with pickup-only items it hides delivery with no explanation or shows a misleading error, and the cart's pickup choice is lost, so orders are abandoned or placed for delivery the shop cannot make.
ideas.description: The merchant tags pickup-only products and writes the message shoppers should see. When the shopper clicks Checkout, the app reads the pickup choice the theme or a calendar app already stored on the cart and sets Shopify's pickup preference, so checkout opens on Pick up at the shop's location. A checkout validation function, which runs on every plan for public apps and also covers express buttons, blocks the Ship path for pickup-only items with the merchant's message. A live cart notice explains the rule before checkout.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of one-location Shopify shops on Basic or Grow (bakeries, butchers, florists, delis and food makers) that sell collection-only items next to items they post.
ideas.buyer: The shop owner, on the business card through Shopify's app billing.
ideas.whyNow: Shopify's ship-and-pickup in one order (June 2026) is for Plus and Enterprise only, checkout UI messages need Plus, and merchants on Basic and Grow posted the problem in September, October and November 2026; the apps that launched in May 2026 have 0 to 2 reviews.

problemEvidence.author: poster B (Shopify user; the account carries a staff-group label, so independence is uncertain)
problemEvidence.summary: Asks Shopify to keep the pickup choice made in the cart and preselect Pick up instead of Ship; there is no native setting and apps add cost. A later post reports a free Storefront API prefill working on Basic.

problemEvidence.author: poster A (owner of a small food business)
problemEvidence.summary: Checkout hides shipping on carts of pickup-only items with no explanation; the owner fixed it with a free cart notice that does not refresh after cart changes.

problemEvidence.author: poster C (store owner on Grow)
problemEvidence.summary: With pickup-only products both Ship and Pickup show, and choosing Ship gives a misleading phone-number error; replies say Grow has no native fix and point to an editable checkout message.

problemEvidence.author: poster D (mobile butcher, employer)
problemEvidence.summary: Offered 250 to 750 GBP for a required delivery-or-collect choice in the cart, saved to the order, on Basic or Grow without Plus; expired, not awarded, and it buys a person rather than software.

Live cart notice

ideas.techStack: Shopify public app: Shopify Functions (cart and checkout validation) deployed with the Shopify CLI, a theme app extension for the cart notice and the pickup preference, a small Node backend on backend-hub for OAuth, webhooks and billing, and a per-app Supabase schema for shop settings.

pricing.rationale: Level with PickupLock ($5.99) and BoomGate ($4.99) and well below BopiSafe ($19.90) and Zapiet ($49.99), because it does the one job those cheaper apps do not: keep the cart's pickup choice.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 shops x $7 a month = $1,050 a month. Assumes App Store search finds it; the exact-niche apps launched in May 2026 have 0 and 2 reviews, so uptake is unknown.
ideas.distribution: First 10: a Shopify App Store listing in the Delivery and pickup category. The Shopify Community's FAQ (https://community.shopify.com/faq) prohibits 'Recommending or promoting apps outside the Ask and Offer board, even when an app is relevant to the question', and on that board members must disclose any commercial relationship. Never reply in the evidence threads.

validationTest.method: A landing page with a '$7 a month, start trial' button and a $60 search-ad test on queries such as 'shopify pickup only products checkout'; in parallel, record PickupLock's and BopiSafe's review counts now and again in 30 days. No outreach to anyone.
validationTest.successCriteria: Ad click-through of at least 3% and at least 8 price-button clicks from 300 visits, or either competitor gaining 5 or more reviews in 30 days.
validationTest.cost: About $60 in ads and a day of work.

ideas.moat: Little: tested behaviour across themes, calendar apps and express checkout is the main edge, and Shopify may extend ship-and-pickup to all plans.
compliance: Shopify app requirements: mandatory privacy webhooks and minimal access scopes.
Consumer law: delivery information must be clear before purchase, which the message supports.
Accessibility: the cart notice is announced to screen readers and meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.

risks.risk: The pickup preference does not reach theme carts, as a Shopify staff reply (2026-06-17) suggests.
risks.mitigation: Spike it on day one on a dev store; if it fails, fall back to a rebuilt Storefront cart or ship validation only.

risks.risk: Shopify extends ship-and-pickup or pickup defaults to Basic and Grow.
risks.mitigation: Keep the app small and cheap and watch the changelog.

risks.risk: PickupLock or BoomGate adds the same feature.
risks.mitigation: Compete on the cart-choice carry-through and one-location simplicity.

scoreRationale.pain: Three on-target merchant threads within 90 days (https://community.shopify.com/t/707284.json, https://community.shopify.com/t/693011.json, https://community.shopify.com/t/694793.json), but two report a free cart notice or text edit as enough.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: The only same-area spend buys a person for a cart choice, posted twice and expired (https://www.freelancer.com/api/projects/0.1/projects/all/?query=shopify%20pickup%20checkout&limit=30&full_description=true&from_time=1782259200), and the exact-niche apps have 2 and 0 reviews (https://apps.shopify.com/pickuplock).
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve through the Shopify App Store's Delivery and pickup category, where PickupLock is listed (https://apps.shopify.com/pickuplock); community promotion is confined to Ask and Offer (https://community.shopify.com/faq).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: PickupLock hides and warns from $5.99, BoomGate blocks by rule free or for $4.99 (https://apps.shopify.com/boomgate), BopiSafe claims the choice holds through checkout (https://apps.shopify.com/bopisafe), and a free recipe is the accepted answer in https://community.shopify.com/t/707284.json.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Validation functions work on all plans for public apps (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/functions/latest/cart-and-checkout-validation.md), but the pickup preference only prefills (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/storefront/latest/objects/CartDeliveryPreference.md) and staff say theme and Storefront carts are separate (https://community.shopify.dev/t/storefront-cart-api-and-shopify-liquid-themes-cart-how-to-make-them-sync/35172).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: No payments beyond Shopify billing and little personal data: the validation function reads cart lines and the delivery method type (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/functions/latest/cart-and-checkout-validation.md); Shopify's privacy webhook rules were not read this run.

review.findings: Re-researched from the watchlist (first seen 2026-11-20): the watchlist gatherer found two more merchant threads, and the researcher confirmed that a public app's validation function can block Ship on every plan while preselecting pickup is only a Storefront API prefill. The adversarial reviewer cut the total from 18 to 16: willingnessToPay 3 to 2 (the paid job was one butcher posting twice for a different task, expired, buying a person; PickupLock has 2 reviews and BopiSafe 0) and competitiveGap 2 to 1 (PickupLock, BoomGate's free rule, BopiSafe's claim and a free recipe in the evidence thread). It found two of five threads off target (a two-location card shop, a florist hiring help for a calendar app) and two later posts by new low-trust accounts that may be app makers, not counted. Re-scoped to carrying a pickup choice already made in the cart into checkout for one-location shops.

missing: pain 3 is below 4: three on-target merchant threads, two of them content with a free fix
willingnessToPay 2 is below 3: no paid app or job for this exact job with buyers
gateGap.closedBy: The ad and landing-page test: 8 or more price-button clicks from 300 visits, or PickupLock or BopiSafe gaining 5 reviews in 30 days, would be the first payment signal (willingnessToPay 3, total 17); with competitiveGap at 1 the gate of 22 is out of reach unless the preselect proves to be something no rival can do.

ideas.summary: For small UK Shopify shops posting to EU customers with Royal Mail: see how checkout, the EU rule and the carrier each count the new 3-euro duty and 2-euro fee, what uplift covers the difference, and which orders cost you money.

public.summary: Find out which EU orders cost you money in the new EU parcel charges, and what to change so they stop.
public.problem: Since July every small parcel you post to an EU customer carries a new flat duty, and since November a handling fee as well. Your checkout, the EU rule and your carrier each count the items differently, and the difference arrives later as a bill from the carrier. You cannot see which orders lost you money or how much to add to your prices.
public.forWhom: Small UK online shops on Shopify that post orders to customers in the EU.
benefits: See which EU orders cost you money
Know how much to add to cover the charges
Spot products missing the codes customs need
A monthly summary instead of surprise bills

ideas.problemStatement: Since 1 July 2026 the EU charges 3 euros per item by tariff classification on parcels of 150 euros or less, and from 1 November 2026 a 2-euro handling fee; Shopify's checkout, the rule and Royal Mail count lines differently, carriers recharge taxes later, and small UK shops learn from the courier's bill that they absorbed the difference.
ideas.description: The app reads the shop's catalogue and EU orders through the Shopify Admin API and lists variants missing an HS code or origin. For each EU order under 150 euros it counts declaration lines the way the rule counts them and the way the carrier counts them, adds the 3-euro duty and the 2-euro handling fee, and compares the result with the duty checkout collected. It suggests the surcharge or currency uplift that would cover the gap, and, where the shop can export its Royal Mail business-account duty statement, matches the carrier's charges to orders. A monthly email lists the orders that cost the shop money.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of small UK Shopify shops (1 to 5 people), such as makers, craft shops and indie publishers, that post orders under 150 euros to EU consumers with Royal Mail delivered-duty-paid on a business account and have Shopify duties turned on.
ideas.buyer: The shop owner, on the business card through Shopify's app billing.
ideas.whyNow: The 3-euro EU duty began on 1 July 2026 and runs to 1 July 2028; product identifiers became mandatory and a 2-euro handling fee per declaration item applies from 1 November 2026 under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2152, and Shopify's own help tells merchants to compare checkout charges with customs charged at destination by hand.

problemEvidence.author: poster A (UK merchant shipping to the EU)

problemEvidence.summary: A 2-euro customs processing fee per declaration item under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2152 from 1 November 2026, on top of the 3-euro duty, with product identifier codes required.

ideas.techStack: Shopify public app with an embedded admin page; Node backend on backend-hub for OAuth, webhooks and billing; a per-app Supabase schema for orders and results; a scheduled job and transactional email for the digest.

pricing.pricePoint: Free line-count check; 9 GBP a month or 79 GBP a year for comparison and the digest (estimate)
pricing.rationale: A shop with 20 EU orders a month absorbing 3 to 5 euros on each loses 60 to 100 euros a month (an estimate, not a merchant's figure); the audit apps charge $7.99 to $14.99 and Zonos $2,500 a year.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 100 shops x 9 GBP a month = 900 GBP a month. Assumes UK shops find it in the App Store and that absorbed charges persist after July's fixes; both are unverified.
ideas.distribution: First 10: a Shopify App Store listing with the keywords 'EU duty', 'Royal Mail DDP' and 'duty recharge'. The Shopify Community allows app recommendations only on the Ask and Offer board, with any commercial relationship disclosed (https://community.shopify.com/guidelines). Never reply in the evidence threads.

validationTest.method: A landing page 'See which EU orders cost you duty' with a 9 GBP a month price button, driven by a 14-day UK search-ad test on 'EU 3 euro duty Shopify' and 'Royal Mail DDP duty charge'; no outreach to anyone.
validationTest.successCriteria: Click-through to the price button of 3% or more and 5 or more sign-ups from shops that say they are on Shopify.
validationTest.cost: About 100 GBP in ads and a day of work.

ideas.moat: A maintained engine for how the rule, Shopify and each carrier count lines, which changes often and which generic duty apps do not track for small UK shops.
compliance: UK GDPR: order addresses are personal data, and Shopify's protected customer data rules apply (not read this run: check before building).
Not customs or tax advice: label every figure an estimate and cite the rule text.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the admin page.

risks.risk: The problem was a launch-week bug that Shopify has fixed, and losses stopped.
risks.mitigation: Wait for a merchant report after 1 November of the 2-euro fee or a recharge being absorbed before building beyond the free check.

risks.risk: No carrier statement format can be imported.
risks.mitigation: Start with the free line-count and uplift check, which needs only Shopify data.

risks.risk: Sources disagree on how the fee is counted (per declaration item or per parcel).
risks.mitigation: Show each count next to its source and let the owner pick the carrier's rule.

scoreRationale.pain: Every report of absorbed duty is dated 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-06, mostly launch-week bugs (https://community.shopify.com/t/644531.json, https://community.shopify.com/t/607782.json); later posts ask only about identifier setup (https://community.shopify.com/t/704809.json).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No paid job or app for reconciliation was found; merchants fixed it free with a 5% currency uplift (https://community.shopify.com/t/644531.json?page=2), and Shopify's fee is for calculation, not reconciliation (https://help.shopify.com/manual/markets/duties-and-import-taxes/charging-duties).
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve through a crowded Shopify App Store search, with ten or more HS-code and identifier apps launched July to October 2026 (https://apps.shopify.com/pidready).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: No app reconciles collected duty against the carrier bill for small shops; Shopify tells merchants to compare by hand (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/duties-and-import-taxes/additional-tasks.md), and the nearest rival covers shipping, not duty (https://apps.shopify.com/oh-ship).
scoreRationale.feasibility: Per-line duties are in the Admin API (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Duty), but carrier duty is invoiced after customs assessment, no usable statement format was found, and sources count the fee differently (https://www.evri.com/news/eu-customs-update-2026).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Reads order personal data and its figures look like customs advice, so it needs estimate labels and Shopify's protected data approval (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Duty).

review.findings: Research narrowed the idea from flagging missing codes (free apps such as PIDReady already do that) to reconciling duty collected at checkout with what the carrier billed, and confirmed it is not the same problem as the published US Duty Price Sheet or Postage Price Check for UK makers. The adversarial reviewer cut the total from 17 to 14: pain 3 to 2 (the 'wiped out our profit' quote the research used was about Norway's VAT scheme, not the EU duty; two poster labels were one account; every absorbed-duty report is from July or early August 2026), willingnessToPay 3 to 2 (the one paid job was unrelated customs paperwork, and merchants fixed it free with a currency uplift) and feasibility 3 to 2 (no Royal Mail or Evri statement with per-parcel duty was found, and Evri and a tax firm count the 2-euro fee differently). It found Oh Ship! as the nearest rival. Re-scoped to shops on Royal Mail delivered-duty-paid with a business account, the 2-euro fee from 1 November and carrier line counting, with a free check first.

missing: pain 2 is below 4: every absorbed-duty report is from July or early August 2026
willingnessToPay 2 is below 3: no paid job or app for this job, and merchants fixed it free with a currency uplift
gateGap.closedBy: The landing-page test (5 or more sign-ups at 9 GBP a month) would be the first payment signal (willingnessToPay 3); promotion also needs a merchant post after 1 November 2026 reporting the 2-euro fee or a recharge being absorbed (pain 3 or 4) and a sample Royal Mail statement that can be imported (feasibility 3), and even then the total stays well below 22.

ideas.title: Duplicate Draft Cleaner for ArtStation Sellers Moving to Gumroad

notes.connected: Connects to the seller's Gumroad account by OAuth to list products, read their state and archive or delete the duplicates the seller confirms.
notes.unattended: A weekly email until 28 February 2027 lists imported drafts still unpublished or unmatched.
notes.engine: Matches imported drafts to existing listings by name, price, permalink and files, and computes net per sale under Gumroad's 10% plus $0.50 fee.

ideas.summary: For ArtStation sellers who already ran a Gumroad store: find the imported drafts that duplicate listings they already have, clean them up safely before 28 February 2027, and see which cheap items the new fees hurt.

public.summary: Tidy up the duplicate products your shop move creates, before the deadline, in minutes instead of an afternoon.
public.problem: Your marketplace is closing and your products arrive in your new store as drafts. If you already sold there, every product you had now appears twice, and you have to find and delete the extra copies by hand, one by one. Miss one and buyers see two versions of the same thing.
public.forWhom: Digital artists moving their brushes, models and tutorials from ArtStation to a Gumroad store they already had.
benefits: Every duplicate found and paired with the original
Clean up in one pass, with nothing deleted until you confirm
See which low-priced items the new fees hurt
A reminder of drafts still waiting before the deadline

ideas.problemStatement: ArtStation's Marketplace checkout closes on 18 December 2026 and products move to Gumroad only as unpublished drafts by 28 February 2027; imports are not merged with existing Gumroad listings, so sellers who already had a Gumroad store must find and delete the duplicates by hand, and their reviews and sales history do not move.
ideas.description: The seller connects their Gumroad account; the tool lists every product with its state and pairs each imported draft with the existing listing it duplicates by name, price, permalink and files. The seller confirms each pair and the tool archives or deletes the extra copy through Gumroad's API, never without confirmation. It also shows net per sale under Gumroad's fee so the seller can reprice items where the fixed $0.50 bites, and a weekly email lists drafts still unpublished until the deadline.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo artists and small studios selling digital products (brushes, 3D models, textures, tutorials) on the ArtStation Marketplace who already ran a Gumroad store.
ideas.buyer: The artist, paying once from their own card.
ideas.whyNow: ArtStation announced on 18 to 20 November 2026 that Marketplace checkout closes on 2026-12-18 and digital products must be moved to Gumroad by 2027-02-28, as drafts that are not merged with existing listings.

problemEvidence.author: ArtStation (vendor help centre)
problemEvidence.summary: Checkout closes 2026-12-18 and digital migration ends 2027-02-28; products arrive as unpublished drafts, imports are not merged with existing Gumroad listings (delete the imported draft), and ratings, reviews, sales history and buyer emails do not transfer.

problemEvidence.author: trade-news author
problemEvidence.summary: Duplicates arrive as extra drafts that must be deleted by hand; Gumroad charges 10% plus $0.50 on direct sales and 30% through Discover.

problemEvidence.author: trade-news editor
problemEvidence.summary: Confirms the move on 2026-12-18 and that artists must move their own listings.

problemEvidence.author: poster A (Fab marketplace creator who bought on ArtStation)
problemEvidence.summary: Asks when Fab will carry the formats bought on ArtStation; shows sellers and buyers looking for a new home, not a complaint about the move's chores.

Weekly reminder of drafts still waiting

outOfScope: Moving ArtStation reviews or sales history (no export exists)

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind front end; Supabase sign-in; the Gumroad OAuth secret exchange and API calls on backend-hub; a scheduled job and transactional email for the weekly reminder; no buyer data stored.

pricing.pricePoint: Free scan; pay what you want with $9 suggested for the clean-up (estimate)
pricing.rationale: A one-time chore for fee-sensitive sellers, with free tools covering everything but the duplicate clean-up; a high price would not sell in a 98-day window.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 sellers x $9 = $1,350 once, before 2027-02-28. Assumes a few hundred sellers with an existing Gumroad store find it by search; the number of affected sellers is unknown.
ideas.distribution: First 10: search ads on 'artstation gumroad migration' and 'artstation marketplace closing' plus a free checklist page. ArtStation sends companies to its paid advertising or recruitment sections rather than artwork posts (https://help.artstation.com/en/articles/16155062); Blender Artists allows one commercial post a month (https://blenderartists.org/t/our-new-policy-on-commercial-posts/1131607). Never post in the evidence thread.

validationTest.method: A landing page 'Clean up your ArtStation-to-Gumroad duplicates' with a free scan and a $9 pay-what-you-want button, promoted by a $75 search-ad test over 7 days before 2026-12-10; no outreach to anyone.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 300 visits, a click-to-price rate of 4% or more, and at least 5 payments or pre-orders.
validationTest.cost: About $75 in ads and a domain.

ideas.moat: None to speak of: a short-lived tool that Gumroad itself could replace; its value is shipping before the deadline.
compliance: GDPR, UK GDPR and CCPA for the seller's account data and OAuth token; request only the product scope and store no buyer data.
Never delete without the seller's confirmation, and log every change.

risks.risk: Gumroad ships duplicate matching or bulk clean-up itself.
risks.mitigation: Ship within days and keep it free to scan; stop when Gumroad does.

risks.risk: Most sellers have few products or no earlier Gumroad store, so the job is small.
risks.mitigation: Target sellers with existing Gumroad stores; the scan shows the count before anyone pays.

risks.risk: A wrong match deletes a real listing.
risks.mitigation: Archive first, delete only on confirmation, and keep an undo list.

scoreRationale.pain: The chores are certain (https://help.artstation.com/en/articles/18442391-artstation-marketplace-migration-seller-faq) but small for a typical catalogue, and the one fetched seller post is about moving to Fab, not the chores (https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/2856883.json).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No paid job or tool for the move was found, free tools cover most of it (https://gumroad.com/mcp), and sellers are fee-sensitive (https://www.tutkit.com/en/news/1147-artstation-marketplace-closes-on-december-18-gumroad-takes-over-sales).
scoreRationale.reachability: Search ads only: ArtStation routes companies to paid advertising (https://help.artstation.com/en/articles/16155062).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Gumroad's free connector lists drafts and publishes (https://gumroad.com/mcp) and Gumroad is building its own migration screens (https://github.com/antiwork/gumroad/pull/8817); only duplicate clean-up is left.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Gumroad OAuth with the edit_products scope (https://gumroad.com/help/article/280-create-application-api) lets an app list, update, enable, disable and delete products, as Gumroad's open-source API code shows (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/antiwork/gumroad/main/app/controllers/api/v2/links_controller.rb).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Holds a store token but no buyer data if it never requests sales scopes (https://gumroad.com/help/article/280-create-application-api).

review.findings: Research confirmed the vendor-mandated chores (drafts, no merge, reviews and history lost) but found no fetched seller complaint about them (seller posts on artstation.com returned 403) and no payment evidence. The adversarial reviewer cut the total from 17 to 14: pain 3 to 2, willingnessToPay 2 to 1 and competitiveGap 3 to 1, because Gumroad's official free connector already lists drafts, sets categories and prices and publishes, Gumroad merged its own migration notices on 2026-11-03, and a free 22-step checklist published on dev.to on 2026-11-19 (URL withheld: it contains a handle) already flags categories; feasibility rose 3 to 4 from Gumroad's open-source API code. It found Lemon Squeezy's wind-down goes to Stripe's own tooling, not a second market. Re-scoped to duplicate matching and clean-up for sellers who already had a Gumroad store, as a free scan with pay-what-you-want clean-up.

missing: pain 2 is below 4: no fetched seller complaint about the move's chores
willingnessToPay 1 is below 3: no payment evidence and free tools cover most of the job
gateGap.closedBy: The 7-day ad test before 2026-12-10: 5 or more payments from 300 visits would be the first payment signal (willingnessToPay 2 or 3); the demand ends on 2027-02-28 and Gumroad may ship the feature, so this ships only as a short-lived lead and cannot reach the gate.

runNotes.caveats: No candidate cleared the quality gate, so four ideas ship as provisional, each with its gap written on it; the best were already crowded or thin. Twenty-three new candidates were scored plus three re-researched watchlist entries (26). Eight candidates went to researchers: two were ended by research (edition register: Artwork Archive and free Shopify tiers; EU withdrawal button off Shopify: free plugins, built-in platform features and hosted embeds), one researcher was stopped unreported once the provisional cap was reached (guest-artist royalties), and five were adversarially reviewed: one killed (DMCC renewal notices for Stripe sellers: two Stripe-specific products already sell it) and four rescored down (batch book 18 to 16, pickup 18 to 16, EU duty 17 to 14, ArtStation move 17 to 14). Review stopped at five reviews because four ideas had survived, the first run's provisional cap. Ideas 3 and 4 ship at 14 under the routine's rule that any reviewed survivor meeting the floor ships up to the cap; both are short-lived leads (the EU duty losses are mostly from July 2026, and the ArtStation move ends on 2027-02-28). Idea 3 serves the same UK makers as the published US Duty Price Sheet (2026-11-08) and Postage Price Check (2026-11-15) but a different problem (reconciling EU duty after the order), as both researcher and reviewer checked. Constraints: small-business buyers in all four (ideas 1 and 2 Small Business Ops, ideas 3 and 4 smallBusiness true); one Weekend MVP (idea 4) and three Multi-week; ideas 1, 2 and 3 are substantial Multi-week with a buildPlan; no category used more than twice. Watchlist: Pickup Preselect shipped as idea 2; POS receipts (18) and the year-end pack (16) were re-researched and left; four carried entries remain, none re-researched today (only the top three are). Every idea's topic is Data & Visualization as the closest fit; the closed list has no topic for shop operations (see the run log's topic request). Evidence URLs that contain a poster's handle (seller blog posts, a dev.to post, a Threads post) are withheld; the facts they would support are cited from vendor pages instead.
